fixtures.purpose: An authored gap refers to a named structural route within one compilation; no revision stability is asserted.
Ordinary prose and non-reserved bracketed text create an empty graph.
Body preserves containment while the marked descendant supports the nearest Point.
Unmarked elaboration produces no Point and no additional support.
A distinction clarifies its enclosing ground; adjacent body produces no connections.
An edge creates a connection but no Point; its body creates neither.
A joint edge uses existing material Points and can receive an undercut with a reply.
An anonymous explicit objection can receive a structural reply.
Forward Point names and route handles resolve without reordering graph entities.
A gap can refer to a named reply connection rather than its enclosing Point.
Body grouping does not change an explicit edge or the undercut targeting it.
A question can remain anonymous while material explicitly refers to its named descendant.
Two single-source supports and one joint support remain exactly three connections.
A named open claim accepts anonymous reasons and objections while context remains body.
Point names and route handles are independently optional and resolve in their proper roles.
Two questions under ordinary groups receive their own answers without cross-group connections.
An explicit challenge replaces a ground role's default support and uses the authored target.
After an explicit Point below an edge, its children resume ordinary structural connections.
An anonymous claim route can receive both an undercut and positive bearing.
A handle cannot create a missing route; the Point survives.
A Bearing cannot be an edge source; its valid base route survives.
Unconnected named material remains a Point and receives a suggestion, not an error.
Both duplicate routes are rejected while all three Points survive.
A repeated source rejects the whole edge rather than silently deduplicating it.
Both duplicate Points and their dependent route are rejected; the independent source Point survives.
The first Point beneath an edge needs an explicit target even through body; its Point still survives the error.
An invalid route handle rejects the attached Bearing but preserves the reason Point.
Unmatched dedents reject apparent annotations until a valid root; the earlier valid ground survives.
One malformed source rejects the entire new edge while an independent about connection survives.
A malformed explicit target rejects the route without falling back to indentation.
Multiple targets reject the attached Bearing; all source and target Points survive.
A Point/handle collision preserves both Points but rejects the conflicting route.
Undercuts require Bearing targets and challenges require Point targets; invalid routes do not enter the graph.
Rejection propagates through route targets while all otherwise valid Points remain.
An unresolved source rejects its whole route.
An unresolved target rejects its whole route.
Names in another fence cannot resolve an explicit target; the local anonymous Point survives.
An empty complete fence is an empty unit with an error rather than an absent unit.
A malformed edge in one fence leaves valid structure in both independent units.
Optional fence indentation preserves host-relative graph locations.
Separate fences can reuse authored names; host prose and non-Cogitatum fences produce no graph.
An unclosed fence is diagnosed and omitted while an earlier complete unit survives.
Explicit operators do not require a name for their source Point.
Malformed reserved prefixes stay body; a valid descendant survives and ordinary brackets remain prose.
Support chains produce no transitive edge; clarifications and replies keep their own kinds.
An ineligible Point blocks ancestor lookup; an explicit role alone does not always imply a connection.
Variable space widths are valid when dedents match active levels.
